The most spectacular exemplar of the Victorian Neo-Gothic style was the Victoria Terminus (VT), the headquarters and terminus of the Great Indian Peninsula Railway. Designed by the British architect F.W. Stevens, its construction began in 1878 and was completed in 1888. Characterized by high-pitched roofs, pointed stone arches, stained glass windows, and intricate carvings of gargoyles and Indian flora and fauna, VT dominated the city skyline.
